questionText:
Consider a matrix $P$ whose only eigenvectors are the multiples of $\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}$.

Consider the following statements.

(I) $P$ does not have an inverse
(II) $P$ has a repeated eigenvalue
(III) $P$ cannot be diagonalized

Which one of the following options is correct?
options: Only I and III are necessarily true
Only I and II are necessarily true
Only II and III are necessarily true
explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the given matrix $P$.
Matrix $P$ is a $2 \times 2$ matrix because its eigenvector is a 2-dimensional vector $\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}$. The problem states that its only eigenvectors are scalar multiples of this vector, meaning $P$ has only 1 linearly independent eigenvector.

Step 2: Evaluate Statement (I) - $P$ does not have an inverse.
A matrix is non-invertible if and only if 0 is an eigenvalue. However, $P$ can have non-zero eigenvalues (for example, $P = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$ is invertible and has a single linearly independent eigenvector). Thus, $P$ can be invertible, making Statement (I) not necessarily true.

Step 3: Evaluate Statement (II) - $P$ has a repeated eigenvalue.
If a $2 \times 2$ matrix had two distinct eigenvalues, it would necessarily have 2 linearly independent eigenvectors. Since $P$ has only 1 linearly independent eigenvector, it must have a repeated eigenvalue. Statement (II) is necessarily true.

Step 4: Evaluate Statement (III) - $P$ cannot be diagonalized.
A matrix of order $n$ is diagonalizable if and only if it has $n$ linearly independent eigenvectors. For matrix $P$, $n = 2$, but it only has 1 linearly independent eigenvector. Therefore, $P$ cannot be diagonalized. Statement (III) is necessarily true.

Hence, only Statements (II) and (III) are necessarily true.
